A path through a wire

Next, Big closed a switch on a battery kit. The lamp lit. A wire is a thin metal path. Some electrons in metal can move along it.

5

Pull or push

“Charge can be positive or negative,” said Big. Opposite charges pull toward each other. Like charges push apart.

4

A few electrons move

Big rubbed a balloon on a wool sweater, then held it near paper bits. A few bits lifted.

3

Too small to see

Little Wonderer studied an atom model under the lamp. An atom is a tiny building block of matter.

2

A sock that stays

A sock stayed on a shirt when Little lifted it. “Static cling!” said Big. That means fabrics stick because of electric charge.

6

Where did they go?

Little drew the sock and shirt, with an arrow for electrons moving between them. “The tiny bits were already there,” Little said.

7

Make a little book

  1. 1Fold it into 8 boxes. Open it flat.

  2. 2Fold short end to short end. Cut the thick line. Open it.

  3. 3Fold the long way, pictures out. Push the ends in.

  4. 4Fold into a book. Page 1 goes on the front!
